sources.title: Planning for extreme heat and heatwaves
sources.page_or_section: Weather forecast districts and corresponding heat health temperature thresholds; Calculating the average temperature; Figure 1
sources.supports: Historical Central District threshold of 30 C and max-plus-following-overnight-minimum daily-mean formula. The page notes this system operated through 2021-22 and is not comparable with the current BOM warning trigger.

sources.title: The impact of heatwaves on mortality in Australia: a multicity study
sources.supports: Melbourne summer daily-mean thresholds of 27.2 C at the 95th percentile and 30.1 C at the 99th percentile, defined for two or more consecutive days.

sources.title: Mapping Heat Health Risks in Urban Areas
sources.page_or_section: Section 2, Materials and Methods; Section 3, Results
sources.supports: Defines Melbourne hot weather using a 30 C 24-hour mean and reports 17% more adverse health outcomes on hot than non-hot summer days in the study period.

daily_mean_air_temperature.prohibited_use: Do not apply these thresholds to a single live BOM observation, apparent temperature, Landsat land-surface temperature or the current national BOM heatwave-warning category.

sources.title: Melbourne's vegetation, heat and land use data
sources.publisher: Victorian Government Department of Transport and Planning
sources.supports: Official metropolitan Melbourne 2018 urban tree-canopy baseline of 15.3%.

sources.title: Action 12: Protect and enhance our canopy trees
sources.publisher: Victorian Government Department of Transport and Planning
sources.supports: Official Plan for Victoria target of 30% tree-canopy cover in urban areas.

canopy_progress.prohibited_use: This is metropolitan baseline/target progress context, not proof of property-level compliance. Do not apply to the current rendered Vicmap canopy proxy; use only after a compatible analytical canopy percentage passes validation.

landsat_surface_heat.method: Versioned 33rd and 66th percentiles of comparable Melbourne application-ready LST cells

sources.title: Urban Vegetation, Urban Heat Islands and Heat Vulnerability Assessment in Melbourne, 2018
sources.publisher: Clean Air and Urban Landscapes Hub / Victorian Government
sources.page_or_section: PDF pages 3 and 5-6: executive summary, introduction and UHI method
sources.supports: Landsat LST is useful as a spatial urban-heat exposure indicator but is not directly equivalent to air temperature and is sensitive to acquisition conditions.

sources.title: FAQ: Bivariate Choropleth Maps
sources.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.page_or_section: What are tertiles?; How are the values associated with tertiles found?
sources.supports: Defines tertiles as three approximately equal rank groups and documents Lowest, Middle and Highest labels.

sources.title: How Calculate Composite Index works
sources.supports: Documents quantile classification as equal-count rank groups and warns that percentile displays preserve rank rather than actual value differences.

landsat_surface_heat.prohibited_use: Do not use the 27.2 C or 30 C air-temperature thresholds for Landsat LST.
